<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **12** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/ai.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/ai.json`, `packages/spec/src/ai/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via schemaId (symbol, a field of const object aiContextForm))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/ai.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/ai.json`, `packages/spec/src/ai/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **176** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json dbc1765a24e953ae52c2a4aa2c600b4b1461ed0d` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `82f189120f4c3d7013a4ada0b61995ce9af3bf6f` — the merge of head `4b6929e4b6886bcb5c66e67f797c5d94c78d7482` into base `dbc1765a24e953ae52c2a4aa2c600b4b1461ed0d`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 82f189120f4c3d7013a4ada0b61995ce9af3bf6f && git checkout 82f189120f4c3d7013a4ada0b61995ce9af3bf6f
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin dbc1765a24e953ae52c2a4aa2c600b4b1461ed0d 4b6929e4b6886bcb5c66e67f797c5d94c78d7482 && git checkout -B drift-repro dbc1765a24e953ae52c2a4aa2c600b4b1461ed0d && git merge --no-ff 4b6929e4b6886bcb5c66e67f797c5d94c78d7482

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json dbc1765a24e953ae52c2a4aa2c600b4b1461ed0d
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs dbc1765a24e953ae52c2a4aa2c600b4b1461ed0d` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `3a215ad95b8a02796c7a192933b666655cc92a28`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/ai/ai-context.form.ts, packages/spec/src/ai/index.ts, packages/spec/src/system/metadata-form-registry.ts, packages/spec/api-surface/ai.json, packages/spec/export-origins/ai.json + ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/widgets.tsx, ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/ContextPackRelatedEntries.tsx
Security-touching: no
Rule-change-verified: none

PR #37315 for card #37143 (ADR-0160 D1 clause 2, row 7). Read: the card body and its three comments (triage 7159949524, claim 7162556031, claim amendment 1 7164603714; no dev report is on the card), the PR body, the 34-file list, the net diff against `main`, and the check-runs on the head (59 success, 10 skipped, none failed or pending). The head is 12 ahead of and 5 behind `main`; none of the 5 commits touches a reviewed file. Code outside the diff was read on `main` at `829a45e9` and in the head tree, never reviewed. The rest of the diff (the two spec/ui test files, the two platform-objects count pins, the generated translation bundles and source hashes, the zh-CN overlay, the studio i18n keys, the readers-table row, the changeset prose) is the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept set of `ai_context`: unchanged. Right.** No hunk touches `ai-context.zod.ts`; `AiContextSchema` still accepts `name`, `label`, `object`, `fields`, `related`, `body` plus the ADR-0010 envelope, and the form offers exactly those six rows (the envelope is the reconciliation gate's `FRAMEWORK_FIELDS` skip). `Test Core` is green on the registry-wide reconciliation.
- **Public surface: one new value export. Right.** `aiContextForm` from `@objectstack/spec/ai` (`index.ts`, one line). `api-surface/ai.json` gains `aiContextForm (const)` and `export-origins/ai.json` gains `src/ai/ai-context.form.ts#aiContextForm (const)`, one line each, and both agree with the source. No type export, no change to `api-surface/system.json`: `METADATA_FORM_REGISTRY` keeps its signature and gains a key.
- **Served surface: `/meta/types` now carries `form` for `ai_context`. Right.** `protocol-meta-type-schema.ts` reads `TYPE_TO_FORM` straight off the registry, so Studio's generic editor moves from the auto-derived single section to this layout. The type was already `allowRuntimeCreate: true` and already placed in Studio's menu (`studioMenuPlacement.ts`, advanced tier); the PR adds no door.
- **i18n extraction: `metadataForms.ai_context` grows from one label to sections and seven rows. Right**, and it is why `ai_context` moves from the bare class to the panel class in the two platform-objects pins (15/18, 26 leaves; positive control 828 to 837). The numbers differ from the forecast in claim amendment 1 (825 to 843) because the base moved and the control counts labels only; the edits are literal counts and a dated comment row, as the amendment allowed.
- **`related-list-entries` now has two faces, chosen by the entry schema. Right.** `isContextPackEntrySchema` wants `items.properties.object` and no `list`. An object's `relatedLists` entry is a name or the closed `{ list, label?, columns? }` object (`RelatedListEntrySchema`, a union that declares no `object` key, and the hand-written fallback schema for `object` names no `relatedLists` at all), so the object form keeps the chip face; the old body is moved under `RelatedListNameEntries` with no other edit (`widgets.tsx` is +26/-1). For a pack, `AiContextRelatedSchema` is a plain closed object under an array (no pipe, no default), so the door's first derivation (output mode) and the `io: 'input'` derivation the new UI test uses give the same `related` node; `maxItems` 3 and `items.properties.fields.maxItems` 10 are read from it.
- **Link resolution agrees with the save-time judge. Right.** `contextPackLinks` and `resolvedLink` use `REFERENCE_VALUE_TYPES` and `referenceTargetOf` the way `packages/lint/src/validate-ai-context.ts` does: a named `field` must point at the root; an omitted one resolves only when the child has exactly one link.

### ② Semver level

`Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` stand line-initial in the PR body and in `.changeset/37143-ai-context-studio-form.md`, and match the tree: a new export and a newly served form widen the public surface; nothing an author can write is added, narrowed or changed in meaning. By AGENTS.md (Post-Task Checklist 3) kind `none` takes `patch`, and a non-protocol widening ships `patch`: the changeset's four `patch` entries (`@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@object-ui/app-shell`, `@object-ui/i18n`) cover every published package the diff moves. `Check Changeset` is green. The level is right.

### ③ Boundary flags

No dev report is on the card (the relay was failing), so the flags are those the PR body carries, plus two read off the tree.

- **End-to-end acceptance covered in pieces; no live Studio run (PR: NOT MEASURED).** Escalated to the seat. The two cited tests exist on `main` (`protocol.runtime-authoring-gate.test.ts`, the `ai_context author defects at save` block; `packages/runtime/src/mcp-record-context-tools-bridge.test.ts`), and the pieces do chain. But nothing in the PR or its check-runs creates or edits a pack through the editor, and S1 below sits exactly in that gap. The card's clause "an author creates a pack in Studio" is unmeasured at this head; a browser pass belongs with the S1 fix.
- **Body picker offers every root field, not only long-text ones.** Answered: consistent. `field-ref` has no type filter, the form says so in its help text, and `validateAiContext` reports `ai-context-body-not-long-text` on the save door (advisory tier, `runtimeTypes: ['ai_context']`).
- **Link catalog is the console's served object list.** Answered: accepted as disclosed. It is the published registry, while each entry's columns come from the draft-overlaid read (`useObjectFields`); a child that exists only as a draft is not offered as a link. The judge also reads published objects, so the two agree. See S2 for the load state.
- **`@object-ui/app-shell` and `@object-ui/i18n` type-check not measured locally; the rest of app-shell's suite left to CI.** Answered by the head: `Type Check UI`, `Test UI` and its 16 shards are green.
- **#37180 soft dependency.** Answered: ADR-0160's cross-reference of 2026-11-25 puts `ai_context` in ADR-0150 bucket 3 beside `skill`; the diff picks no package, as the PR says.
- **Claim amendment 1, the two count pins.** Answered under ①: counts and a dated comment only.
- **File surface, read off the tree.** For the seat's L1: the claim names i18n keys under `ui/packages/i18n/src/locales/**`; the diff writes them to `ui/packages/i18n/src/namespaces/studio/en.ts` and `zh.ts`, which is where `engine.form.*` lives. Same intent, a path the claim did not name.
- **SQL push-down.** No finding. The diff adds no record query, no id materialisation and no in-app join over records. Its one new read is the browser's read of the whole object registry (`useMetadata().objects`) to find the reference fields that point at the root; that is metadata, and the PR classifies the reader `off` in `openPathObjectReaders-12811.test.ts`.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/ai/ai-context.form.ts`** — against ADR-0160 D1, `AiContextSchema`, and its first consumer (`ResourceEditPage`, `SchemaForm`, `widgets.tsx` at the head).

Holds: the six rows are the schema's six keys; `name` is required and immutable, `label` and `object` required, as the schema requires them; every help text repeats a sentence the schema or the judge already says (the bounds come from the exported constants, not from copies); the jsdoc's claim that defects are reported at save and bounds refused at parse is true of `validate-ai-context.ts` (advisory) and of `protocol-save.ts` (422 `INVALID_METADATA` on a failed parse). The root pickers do get the root's fields: `ResourceEditPage` binds `context.objectFields` to `draft.object`. A create draft starts with none of the optional keys (`ai_context` has no create seed), so an untouched `fields`, `related` or `body` is absent and the pack saves.

S1 (should-fix) — two ordinary edits leave a draft the save door refuses, with no way back in the form. `AiContextSchema.fields` is `min(1)` and `body.field` is a required identifier, but the form routes both to generic blocks that write the empty value instead of removing the key:
- `fields` through `field-multi`: removing the last chip calls `onChange([])` (`widgets.tsx` L2236-2239 at the head); `SchemaForm.setField` deletes a key only for `undefined` or `''` (L1260), so the draft holds `fields: []` and the save is answered 422.
- `body.field` through `field-ref` inside a composite: the picker's own "None" item calls `onChange('')` (`widgets.tsx` L2078); `CompositeField` writes it back as-is (`SchemaForm.tsx` L2761), so the draft holds `body: { field: '' }` and the save is answered 422 on an identifier rule ("at least 2 characters") for an author who chose None.
The console has no `fromDraft` for `ai_context` and no client validator for it, so nothing prunes or pre-empts either. A pack with no `fields`, or with no `body`, is a legal pack; once either key was touched, the form cannot return to it and the author needs the Source tab. The PR closes this very case for `related` and for a list's columns, and gives the reason ("both arrays are `minItems: 1`"); the two rows beside them are left open. The `page.form.ts` precedent does not carry over, because its `columns` has no lower bound. A fix can live in the console (the two generic blocks honouring an optional key, or a `fromDraft` for the type) or in the form's choice of blocks.

N1 (nit) — `dependsOn: 'object'` on `fields` and on `body.field` has no reader: `field-multi` and `field-ref` take their catalog from `context.objectFields`, never from `dependsOn` (only `related-list-entries`, `field-selector` and the dynamic-config block read it). Inside the `body` composite the form data handed down is `body` itself, so `object` there names no sibling. The scoping is real, but it comes from `ResourceEditPage`; the spec test "scopes every field picker by the root object" pins the declaration, not the scoping. Same shape as the `page.form.ts` precedent; no effect today.

**`packages/spec/src/ai/index.ts`, `packages/spec/src/system/metadata-form-registry.ts`, `api-surface/ai.json`, `export-origins/ai.json`** — hold. One named export beside `skillForm`; one registry key after `skill`, importing through `../ai` as its neighbours do; the two generated declarations match. Nothing to grade.

**`ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/widgets.tsx`** (implementing) — holds. The dispatcher calls no hook, reads the root from the row its `dependsOn` names in the root draft (the row is top-level, so `formData` is the draft), and hands the naming props to the one control the pack face always renders, which keeps the widget's `control` labelling true in every state.

**`ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/ContextPackRelatedEntries.tsx`** (implementing) — agrees with the form's jsdoc sentence by sentence on what it writes: a pick is `{ object, field }`; columns come from that child; an edit replaces only `fields` and keeps every other stored key (so row 11's `where`, `orderBy`, `limit` will survive an edit here); an emptied column set or list removes its key; adds stop at the schema's bounds; an entry the catalog shows no link for is kept and marked. I could not make it write a value `AiContextSchema` refuses.

S2 (should-fix) — the link catalog has no load state, so "not loaded" and "load failed" are drawn as "no links". `useMetadata().objects` starts the whole-registry fetch on first read and returns the items in hand, an empty list until it lands (`MetadataProvider.readType`). The component reads it at L255-256 and never asks `getTypeStatus('object')`. Until the registry arrives, the add picker says "No object has a reference field that points at the root object" and every stored entry carries the amber "No reference field to the root: reported when saved"; if the load fails, both stay, and the second is a verdict the save will not give. Nothing wrong is written (entries are kept). The same file draws loading and failure for a child's columns, and `widgets.tsx` states the rule this breaks in its own comments (objectui#5170: an unanswered question renders as asking, a failed load is never an answer of none).

N2 (nit) — a stored entry with no `field` whose child has several links to the root is marked "No reference field to the root", while the judge's sentence for that case is that the child has several and `field` must name one; the entry also hides both of that child's links from the add picker until it is removed.

N3 (nit) — a list's columns can be added and removed but not reordered, while the schema reads them "in order" and the root `fields` block does offer reordering.

N4 (nit) — nothing ties the pack face to `AiContextRelatedSchema`'s keys: the form's `related` row declares no sub-rows, so the reconciliation gate does not walk the entry. When row 11 (card #37203) adds `where`, `orderBy` and `limit`, the block will not offer them and no gate will say so. A follow-up for that card, not for this PR.

Two should-fix (S1, S2), four nits, no must-fix. S1 and S2 are open on this head and each earns a delta review of its fix.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `6ada5fd590d9bd594eb8e128a2ec3b0c77cdada4`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/ai/ai-context.form.ts, packages/spec/src/ai/index.ts, packages/spec/src/system/metadata-form-registry.ts + ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/SchemaForm.tsx, ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/widgets.tsx, ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/ContextPackRelatedEntries.tsx, ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/ContextPackRelatedEntries-37143.test.tsx, .changeset/37143-ai-context-studio-form.md
Security-touching: no
Rule-change-verified: none

Delta round on PR #37315 (card #37143), after the round-1 record in PR comment 7167828479 (head `3a215ad9`, S1 and S2 open). Read: that record, the dev's rework report (card comment 7169483447), the compare `3a215ad9...6ada5fd5` (2 commits, 5 files, +135/-10), the five files at the head, the PR body, and the check-runs on the head. The three `hits` paths are in no delta hunk: the compare lists no file under `packages/spec/**`, so they are byte-identical to the head round 1 reviewed and its judgment of them stands. The five paths after `+` are the whole delta. Code outside the diff was read on `main` at `829a45e9` and in the head tree (`MetadataProvider.tsx`, `AppShellContext.tsx`, `protocol-meta-type-schema.ts`, the twelve `*.form.ts` files that declare a composite, `view.zod.ts`, `ObjectGrid.tsx`, `ListView.tsx`), never reviewed.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept set of `ai_context`: unchanged. Right.** No file under `packages/spec/**` is in the delta. `AiContextSchema` at the head still reads `fields` as an array of 1 to 8 distinct names, optional, and `body` as the closed object whose one key `field` is required, optional as a whole.
- **Public surface: no new export. Right.** The delta adds four module-level exports: `compositeWith` (`SchemaForm.tsx`), `emptyArrayRefused` (`widgets.tsx`), `catalogStateOf` and the type `ContextPackCatalogState` (`ContextPackRelatedEntries.tsx`). None is reachable from `@object-ui/app-shell`: the package's `exports` map holds `.` and `./styles.css` only, and `src/index.ts` at the head re-exports `SchemaForm` by name alone from that module. `@objectstack/spec` is untouched.
- **What the editor writes changes in three places, two of them generic.** (1) `field-multi`: removing the last chip of an array whose schema node has `minItems` of 1 or more writes `undefined`, not `[]`. (2) `CompositeField`: a sub-field cleared to `undefined` or `''` drops its key. (3) `CompositeField`: a composite left with no key, whose schema node has a non-empty `required`, is written as `undefined`. (1) and (2) are right for every form I read; (3) is right for the pack and wrong in reach, see S3.
  - Reach of (1): every `field-multi` row, declared (`ai_context.fields`, `page.form.ts` `columns`) or auto-detected (a string array named `*Fields`, `columns`, `fieldOrder`). It fires only where `[]` is a value the save refuses, so no legal value is lost: an optional array returns to absent, a required one (`TimesheetConfigSchema.rowFields`, `min(1)`) trades one refusal for another. `add` and `move` are unchanged, and an array with no lower bound still writes `[]` (pinned).
  - Reach of (2): the 56 declared composite rows in 12 forms on `main`, plus the pack's `body`. The builtin text and number inputs already answer a cleared box with `undefined` (`SchemaForm.tsx` L2581, L2606, L2618), so the only value newly dropped is the `''` a registered widget writes: `field-ref`'s "None" and the pickers' failure-arm text boxes. An empty field name is never a legal value, and `SecretWidget` clears with `null`, not `''`, so its protocol is untouched.
  - Every host of a composite takes `undefined`: `setField` deletes the key, a parent composite deletes it through `compositeWith`, and a repeater or record row keeps an `undefined` member that serialisation drops (the convention `SchemaForm.tsx` L2259-2262 already states). A composite is never a scalar list element.
- **The link catalog now has three states. Right.** `MetadataTypeStatus` is `idle`, `loading`, `ready`, `error`; `getTypeStatus` is optional on the context and its contract reads "absent means always ready". `catalogStateOf` maps absent and `ready` to ready, `error` to error, and the rest to loading.

### ② Semver level

`Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` still stand line-initial in the PR body (L6-7) and in the changeset (L10-11), and still match the tree: the delta adds no export, no served key and no accepted value. The changeset keeps its four `patch` entries and gains two bullets for the rework; every source file of the delta is in `@object-ui/app-shell`, already listed. `Check Changeset` is green on the head. The level is right. The second sentence of the first new bullet is narrower than the code, see S3.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Rework report, deviation "the rework widens the change to two generic editor behaviours, both schema-driven".** Answered in ① and ④: the `field-multi` behaviour holds; the composite removal reads a keyword that does not mean what its comment says on the served schema, S3.
- **Rework report, `open_questions`: empty.** Nothing to answer.
- **Round-1 escalation, no live Studio run.** The report now claims one at the rework source (create, edit, body then "None", both root fields removed, publish 200 each time, `get_record_context` answering the pack) with evidence under `/mnt/project-files/seat7/37143-dogfood/`. I did not read that evidence; the claim agrees with the code path I read. The seat's to accept.
- **Rework report, the ablation pass first run on uncommitted edits and redone on the committed head.** Not a contract question; the seat's L1.
- **Check-runs on the head, noted and not judged:** 72 runs, 59 success, 12 skipped, 1 in progress: `Test UI (5/16)`, started 17:27:58Z, the re-run of the shard the report names (a failure in `ui/packages/auth`, outside the diff). No aggregate `Test UI` run was listed at the time of the read. `Type Check UI`, the other fifteen `Test UI` shards, `Test Core` and its ten shards, and `Check Changeset` are green.
- **SQL push-down.** No finding. The delta adds no query, no id materialisation and no join. Its one new read is `getTypeStatus('object')`, which the provider documents as a pure read of an in-memory status that starts no fetch.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/ai/ai-context.form.ts`, `packages/spec/src/ai/index.ts`, `packages/spec/src/system/metadata-form-registry.ts`** — unchanged in the delta; the round-1 judgment stands, N1 with it. Against the first consumer at this head the form's two generic rows now behave as the schema needs:

S1: closed. `FieldRefMultiWidget` now takes `schema` (the node `FieldControl` hands every registered widget, L2358) and `removeAt` writes `undefined` when the array would be empty and `emptyArrayRefused(schema)`; `setField` deletes the key. `removeAt` is the only writer that shrinks the list. For `body`, `compositeWith` drops the `''` that "None" writes, finds the object empty with `required: ['field']`, and returns `undefined`; `setField` deletes `body`.
